description:
Implement data minimization for local search and narrow install-time permissions using the completed background/runtime audit as evidence.

- In `meridian.js:647-654` and `components/sidebar.js:367-374`, load enabled `localSearch` sources before querying and invoke only enabled tab/bookmark/history searches; do not query then filter.
- Audit `manifest.json:13-14` against actual background and UI API use. Remove unused `scripting`. Where technically viable, move `<all_urls>`, bookmarks, and history to optional permission flows tied to explicit user actions/settings. If a persistent permission is essential, document the exact user-facing justification.
- Preserve clear behavior for denied/revoked optional permissions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Disabled sources trigger no underlying API query.
- Manifest permissions are the minimum demonstrated by shipped behavior.
- Optional-permission enable, denial, and revocation paths are tested where introduced.
- README/privacy/listing guidance matches the resulting permissions.
## Reviewer rework requirements (July 26, 2026)

1. `utils/localSearch.js:getEnabledLocalSearchSources()` must require both the saved toggle and the optional permission. The current `if (stored[source] === false) return` logic enables bookmarks/history when the saved value is absent but an old grant remains, contradicting the disabled-by-default policy. Add a regression for an absent preference plus a present grant.
2. Do not silently delete shipped page-metadata search to remove `scripting`. The audit confirmed `chrome.scripting` was actively extracting meta descriptions/headings. Restore that behavior and permission, or implement an explicitly optional content-indexing design that preserves informed user choice and equivalent documented behavior. Update tests and privacy/README claims to match the chosen behavior.
label: Maintenance
title: Gate local search data access and minimize extension permissions

activity.content:
## Completed

- Local-search callers now resolve effective source settings and optional grants before search, and the shared search engine invokes only enabled tab, bookmark, or history providers.
- Bookmark/history access moved from install-time permissions to explicit optional permission requests in Settings and the scoped-search buttons. Denials remain off, disabling removes grants, and browser-side revocation updates saved state and active results.
- Removed `scripting` plus DOM metadata/headings extraction. Existing indexes are rebuilt without those fields.
- Retained `<all_urls>` only for automatic visible-tab thumbnail capture, with the exact `activeTab` limitation documented in README and privacy/store-listing guidance.
- Mirrored every runtime/manifest change into `meridian-extension/`.

## Verification

- `node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/*.test.mjs` - 36 passed, 0 failed.
- `node --check` - every shipped JavaScript file parses.
- `git diff --check` - clean.
- Source/package SHA-256 parity - all changed mirrored files match.

Changes requested: optional sources can become enabled with no saved opt-in when an old permission grant exists; the task also removed active page-metadata search without product approval. See appended rework requirements.

## Completed

- Optional bookmark/history search now requires both an explicit saved `true` preference and the corresponding Chrome permission. Missing preferences remain disabled even if an old grant exists, and no permission inspection or underlying search occurs for those sources.
- Restored the shipped one-shot page metadata extractor for completed tabs in both source and packaged trees. Meta descriptions and H1/H2 headings are retained in the local tab index and contribute to search scoring.
- Restored the required installed `scripting` permission while keeping `bookmarks` and `history` optional. Persistent `<all_urls>` and `scripting` are documented with the exact automatic thumbnail/metadata-indexing justification.
- Updated README, privacy/store-listing guidance, release validation notes, manifest assertions, optional-permission regression coverage, and metadata-extraction coverage.

## Verification

- `node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/*.test.mjs` - 43 passed, 0 failed.
- `node --check` - all 40 shipped JavaScript files parsed.
- Source/package SHA-256 parity - all changed mirrored files match.
- `git diff --check` - clean.
